Four-pass audit closure and explicit limitations: [#15](https://github.com/imxade/DOC/issues/15#issuecomment-7152198991).

All new DOC implementation belongs to `runtime-doc/` with DOC-authored compiler/runtime/stdlib/tests; shared CI may build and compare the immutable reference. #11 begins under the already authorized automatic handoff. This is NOT Stage-1/Stage-2 completion. Maintain mandatory independent no-GC/no-RC safety, cancellation/retirement, source/graph epochs, native system/freestanding proof, generated C/WGSL, measured placement, placed-profile obligations (see #7), and #14 final reproducible release gates. No schedule.

## Binding authorization: automatic start after #24 and #15 (2026-11-24)

User now explicitly authorizes #11 implementation **without another permission check**, immediately after #24 is resolved and #15's four-pass reconciliation is verified on the accepted exact SHA. Until then #11 remains blocked, not started. At handoff record the exact frozen Rust reference revision; preserve `runtime-rust/` intact, and begin all new DOC-authored compiler/runtime/stdlib/test implementation in `runtime-doc/`. Continue through #11 acceptance rather than stopping when ready. This supersedes all earlier pause/await-authorization/stop-at-readiness wording only; every technical and safety gate, separate-source architecture and release policy remains binding.

## Binding implementation separation and Rust freeze (2026-11-24)

User explicitly requires two independent implementations to coexist in the development repository. Finish #24 and #15 in `runtime-rust/` as planned; at their verified handoff, record the exact accepted SHA and **freeze Rust in its existing directory** (including its partial #11 Stage-0 AOT work, reference runtime, tests and bootstrap tooling). Do not replace, move, remove or rewrite that implementation during self-hosting. It remains an independent optional bootstrap/reference oracle. Any necessary post-freeze Rust bootstrap repair requires explicit user approval, documented justification and separate revalidation.

All new #11 compiler and portable runtime implementation, standard library and native conformance tests must live in the separate [`runtime-doc/` directory](https://github.com/rtu0/doc2/tree/main/runtime-doc), authored in DOC, with compiler/runtime/stdlib/tests subdirectories as real sources are added. Subsequent implementation development targets DOC only, not both runtimes. Shared specifications, engine/application source, CI and independent conformance fixtures may remain at their existing appropriate repository locations. Stage 0 bootstraps Stage 1; Stage 1 compiles the same DOC source to Stage 2; final self-hosted compiler and applications neither link nor invoke the Rust evaluator. Generated C via Clang/GCC and generated WGSL via WebGPU remain backend outputs, with narrow external platform/toolchain interfaces as previously specified. Preserve all existing semantic, safety, no-GC/no-RC, hardware and native self-bootstrap acceptance requirements.

The later curated independent release excludes the original Rust evaluator as a runtime dependency/distribution component; this does **not** authorize deletion of Rust from the development repository. Earlier language about replacing Rust means replacing its role as the active implementation, not replacing its source tree.

Repository handoff boundary established by [commit d8e1d76](https://github.com/rtu0/doc2/commit/d8e1d76e65a4ae102b3692335a6777687016f550). Its latest binding scope narrows acceptance to genuine foundational gaps, small constructive demonstrations and native proof. Full OS/driver/timer/DMA/peripheral subsystems, library ecosystems and C++ feature parity are NOT required before #11 when implementable in DOC afterward. No arbitrary target/hardware support or weakening DOC's high-level dependency model, memory safety or no-GC/no-RC commitments. #21 remains one small 3D game with DOC-generated graphics and compute WGSL, not a graphics-engine feature-completeness exercise. #15 audits only the accepted foundations and fixes actual blockers; #11 self-hosts and revalidates them. Sequence #21 → #24 → #15 → #11 unchanged; keep #11 paused until all prerequisite gates pass and user authorizes resumption.

This supersedes prior sequencing wording, not substantive acceptance or memory-safety requirements.

#11 remains paused. First complete [#21](https://github.com/imxade/DOC/issues/21) with one actual 3D game and DOC-authored compute and graphics kernels lowered to WGSL. Then reconcile and complete [#15](https://github.com/imxade/DOC/issues/15)'s four-pass pre-bootstrap audit and address findings. Only then mark #11 ready, notify the user, and await explicit permission to resume. Preserve generated GPU kernels, graphics and all accepted engine behavior through self-hosting, with no GC/RC in DOC-managed lifetimes. Final post-bootstrap audit remains required.

---

Public development tracking for [canonical DOC Issue #11](https://github.com/imxade/DOC/issues/11). **Prerequisite public #1 / canonical #22 is verified and closed; ready for implementation.** Original issue numbering remains the canonical reference.

## Chosen AOT backend — DOC → generated C → native executable (2026-11-23)

**Binding implementation target for #11:** `.doc` → DOC parsing/type checking and typed dependency IR → **generated C source** → **Clang or GCC** (object code + optimization/linking) → **standalone native Linux x86_64 executable**, containing only the necessary compiled DOC semantic support plus narrowly scoped system/WebGPU libraries. **C is the *code-generation intermediate target*, not the user-facing language, a separate virtual machine, or a second DOC runtime.** The end user's compiled application executes machine code directly; it does not need a C compiler, Rust DOC evaluator, Goose, bytecode VM, or resident DOC interpreter at runtime. Clang/GCC and a linker are **build-time** tools.

**Why C:** Let a mature C compiler/toolchain own instruction selection, register allocation, machine-code optimization, ELF/object generation, linking and ordinary C/OS/WebGPU ABI integration. That reduces bespoke compiler/backend engineering during the Rust-bootstrap → DOC-self-hosting transition. C itself provides low-level allocations, synchronization/threads and libraries, **not** DOC's automatic dependency parallelism, reactive invalidation, demand/recurrence, source/graph epochs, memory/resource safety, effects or all-or-nothing publication. Those semantics remain DOC's responsibility and must be preserved by generated/specialized C code and/or a **DOC-authored support library compiled to native object code and bundled/statically linked with each executable**. Small native OS, threading and WebGPU ABI bindings may remain external; no separate installed DOC VM/runtime is required.

**Keep a backend-neutral typed DOC IR:** The compiler should determine typed values, checked errors/overflow, dependency-frontier plans, incremental invalidation, source/graph version tokens, effects and publication rules **before** C emission. C emission must be deterministic, namespaced, avoid undefined behavior (signed overflow, out-of-bounds access, invalid lifetime, data races and unspecified evaluation order), and preserve all needed barriers/checks. For static dependency graphs, emit specialized native functions, minimal metadata and precomputed schedules. For dynamic/reactive graphs, compile in the actual update scheduler, invalidation/repair logic and safe reclamation/atomic publication. Do not implement an interpreter loop merely because some graph operations are dynamic.

**CPU + GPU:** C-generated native host code runs DOC's CPU execution and runtime semantics. For explicit `--backend=gpu`, the executable's CPU-side WebGPU adapter creates a device, manages buffers/pipelines, dispatches WGSL kernels for eligible pure work, waits for validated readback and commits complete epochs; the kernels do not replace DOC host orchestration, graph scheduling, effects or device-lifetime guards. CPU remains the default; no hidden GPU→CPU fallback. WebGPU is an external implementation/driver dependency where actually used, not a requirement for CPU-only programs.

**Bootstrap sequence:** (0) Current Rust implementation emits C for a small real typed DOC subset and invokes Clang/GCC to produce a working native binary, checked against Rust semantics and negatives; (1) progressively implement the compiler and portable runtime-support algorithms **in DOC**, using Stage 0 to produce native binaries; (2) that native DOC-authored compiler emits C and compiles **its own DOC source** into a new native compiler, reproducing behavior in Stage 1→Stage 2; (3) DOC user programs compile to independent native CPU binaries and optionally GPU-enabled binaries, without linking or invoking the Rust DOC evaluator. The Rust prototype is retained as trusted bootstrap/reference until proven replaceable, not shipped as the permanent release evaluator. Goose is deprecated as an active requirement under the current Rust-only scope.

**Acceptance criteria for choosing C, not merely naming it:**
- [ ] From an unchanged `.doc` input, generate inspectable C, invoke Clang or GCC, and obtain a real native executable **without an embedded DOC interpreter/VM**; verify executable linkage and clean-environment startup.
- [ ] Test checked arithmetic, types, dependency frontiers, automatic parallelism, repeated input changes, demand/recurrence, graph repair/epochs, safe lifetime, effect ordering, cancellation and **atomic publication** across reference execution and AOT. Unsupported subsets must fail explicitly; a one-shot scalar success does not prove full DOC semantics.
- [ ] Compile/link only required DOC-authored runtime support modules (and minimal native platform adapters); record binary size, generated C size, build time, RSS and cold/steady execution performance. Do not conflate static bundling with eliminating runtime *behavior*.
- [ ] For selected GPU operations, prove real WebGPU/WGSL dispatch/readback and failure semantics from the native executable; label Mesa/software evidence separately from physical GPU.
- [ ] Reproduce Stage-0→Stage-1→Stage-2 self-bootstrap with the same DOC compiler source and no original Rust/Goose DOC evaluator dependency in final executables.
- [ ] Keep LLVM IR/QBE/direct machine-code emission **out of initial implementation scope**. Reconsider a different native backend only with measured C-specific correctness, optimization, compile-time or maintenance limitations and a documented decision; do not build multiple speculative backends.

**Sequencing:** Make the C-target design explicit **now**, but land it as small verified vertical slices alongside current Rust DOC semantics/WebGPU acceptance rather than replacing working production source prematurely. [#14](https://github.com/imxade/DOC/issues/14) remains the clean public self-hosted release gate; that public snapshot must not ship deprecated Goose or original Rust evaluator code. This issue update makes **no claim that C code generation or self-hosting is implemented yet**.


The current Rust DOC reference source and versioned typed IR are migrated to rtu0/doc2. This is a tracking issue, not a claim of C compilation or self-hosting implementation.

## Readiness — 2026-11-24

The prerequisite is now satisfied: canonical [#22](https://github.com/imxade/DOC/issues/22#issuecomment-7122217439) and public [#1](https://github.com/rtu0/doc2/issues/1#issuecomment-7122216205) closed completed. Sole branch `rtu0/doc2/main` exact SHA `0f186a8a1b5d71023f6d19100d1ed4ad16a49c5b` passed [Linux CPU/software-WebGPU 2/2](https://github.com/rtu0/doc2/actions/runs/45323487472) and [physical Tesla T4 automatic mixed gameplay and selected GPU validation](https://github.com/rtu0/doc2/actions/runs/45323904580). Preserve automatic DOC independence, device placement, atomic semantics and correctness as AOT requirements. #11 is READY, not started; proceed only on user's explicit next instruction. Work directly on main; no extra branches.

## Issue #11 implementation started — Stage 0

User authorized implementation after #22 closure. Single active branch `rtu0/doc2/main`; baseline `0f186a8` had green Linux and physical Radar Chase proof. [Stage-0 candidate b8f3e83](https://github.com/rtu0/doc2/commit/b8f3e837d26e4a38851b8b92e6277f8d772385dd) adds `doc-compile`, deterministic specialized C functions for scalar int/bool DOC graphs, checked signed arithmetic, lazy if, dependency levels, bounded real pthreads, demand closure, incremental exact-cutoff updates and private candidate publication, carry/fact recurrence and strict rejection of unsupported types/effects or compiled GPU selection. Canonical typed IR is exported alongside generated C; native ELF compiled by GCC/Clang, no embedded interpreter. Tests compare actual Rust vs compiled output including negatives, 1/2/4/8 worker controls, repeat updates, demand, recurrence and independent launch without source or evaluator. CI records ELF/linkage, size and time/RSS. [Exact candidate CI](https://github.com/rtu0/doc2/actions/runs/45329054988) is running; no execution-pass claim yet. [Architecture and limits](https://github.com/rtu0/doc2/blob/b8f3e837d26e4a38851b8b92e6277f8d772385dd/docs/DOC-AOT.md).

Continue Stage 0 validation/expansion to full necessary typed values/IR, dynamic runtime and effect semantics, compiled WebGPU host orchestration with real physical evidence; then implement portable compiler/runtime in DOC, native Stage 1→Stage 2 self-bootstrap and clean-checkout independent applications. Preserve #22 acceptance and keep #11 open until the entire contract is verified. No interpreter masquerading as AOT, no second language, no native backend detour.

## Binding Issue #11 exit gate — compile and run the existing DOC engine and game (2026-11-24)

The user requires end-to-end acceptance of the **existing DOC-authored engine and actual Radar Chase game**, not a new toy or rewritten host-language surrogate. The already accepted #10/#22 implementation and [exact reference revision 0f186a8](https://github.com/rtu0/doc2/commit/0f186a8a1b5d71023f6d19100d1ed4ad16a49c5b) are the baseline; [native CPU/software-WebGPU reference](https://github.com/rtu0/doc2/actions/runs/45323487472) and [physical Tesla T4 reference](https://github.com/rtu0/doc2/actions/runs/45323904580) establish comparison evidence, not AOT evidence. This gate is **mandatory for closing #11**, independent of whether the game is bundled in the curated #14 public release.

- [ ] Use the final self-hosted DOC compiler (native Stage 2, not merely the Rust Stage-0 prototype) to compile the existing engine, its actual DOC modules, `engine/radar_chase.doc` and typed data/assets through the agreed DOC → typed IR → generated C → GCC/Clang → native executable path. Preserve source-level game rules and feature coverage; any necessary semantics-preserving migration must be justified and differentially tested, not a host-side gameplay rewrite or a simplified replacement. Native platform I/O, threading and WebGPU bindings may remain minimal documented substrate.
- [ ] Build the game from a clean checkout using the self-hosted compiler; execute the resulting native binary in an isolated clean Linux x86_64 environment **without the Rust/Goose DOC evaluator, a DOC interpreter/VM, source parser, or hidden evaluator process/library**. Verify actual binary linkage, loaded dependencies and process invocation; the original Rust runtime is only an external differential oracle during validation. The native game must not need the C compiler at runtime.
- [ ] Repeat the real #22 full winning replay `edsssxwddddsspr` and compare complete frame/entity/radar and typed-state/effect outputs with the accepted Rust oracle. Validate real spawn/despawn/identity/collision/query, prefab/typed asset loading and safe reload, fixed-step input/timers/animation, score/win at tick 13, pause/restart, save/load/restore, replay and WAV-file audio effects. Exercise resource capacity, stale handles, malformed assets/checkpoints, checked failures, graph/epoch safety and atomic publication. No weaker reduced gameplay subset substitutes for the existing engine.
- [ ] Demonstrate automatic workload scaling/placement from DOC dependency independence in the **compiled game**, not only in a microbenchmark. With the same unannotated game source, verify CPU-only execution, actual native CPU thread concurrency under 1/2/4/8 requested-worker controls and default detection, hardware availability/core and ready-frontier bounds, automatic mixed CPU/WebGPU execution on a genuine supported physical GPU, and honest CPU-only fallback in auto mode when a compatible device is absent. Explicit GPU selection must still fail closed if unsupported. No game-level worker/device/partition/scheduling directives or handcrafted GPU workload split.
- [ ] Prove real mixed same-epoch CPU/GPU compute (not graphics rendering) with native scheduler/dispatch/readback traces, actual per-frontier workload breakdown, physical adapter identity, device/limit admission, resource reuse, and complete replay parity with the CPU oracle; separately label software WebGPU CI. For the reference replay the #22 baseline is 2,940 derived evaluations across 15 successor epochs, with 930 CPU + 2,010 GPU and 15 mixed frontiers. Report actual compiled counts, explain any legitimate optimization-induced differences, and verify actual CPU and GPU work remains present. Inject CPU/GPU failure and validate that no partial successor frame/state/effect publication occurs.
- [ ] Record build/compile time, C/native binary size, actual linked libraries, CPU and mixed latency distributions, peak memory, cold/warm device initialization and reuse, measured automatic scaling across workers/frontier sizes and hardware, and limitations. No universal speedup promise; the prior small game was slower on GPU, and profitability policy must remain honest. Preserve native Linux CPU/software-WebGPU CI and separate exact-source physical-GPU proof.
- [ ] Attach reproducible commands, source and compiler SHAs, native binary digests, real logs, comparison outputs and regression-test results to #11 and its public tracker. Re-run required checks on the exact accepted revision. **Do not close #11** until Stage 1→Stage 2 self-hosting, standalone runtime semantics and this native-engine/game acceptance all pass. GUI/editor, generated art and 3D remain deferred #21.

These requirements extend rather than replace #11's existing compiler, semantic and self-hosting acceptance criteria. #22 remains closed for its reference-runtime validation; successful execution through that existing Rust runtime alone cannot fulfill this new gate.

## Binding memory-management architecture and exit gate — 2026-11-24 (resolution of #13)

The user adopts a mandatory collector-free and reference-counting-free DOC value lifecycle for the final self-hosted compiler, compiled support runtime and native applications. This supersedes the optional future policy review in [#13](https://github.com/imxade/DOC/issues/13). Preserve all existing DOC semantic and safety guarantees; do not trade correctness or feature coverage for the absence of a memory-management mechanism.

- [ ] No programmer-written lifetime annotations, borrow-checker obligations, explicit memory allocation/free, GC controls or reference-count bookkeeping in DOC source, including DOC-authored compiler/runtime algorithms. No DOC borrow-checking system or tracing/cycle garbage collector, and no runtime reference counting (including atomic/shared-pointer/retain-release variants) to govern DOC value, snapshot, graph-generation or managed-resource lifetimes. Do not move forbidden mechanisms behind generated C, an FFI wrapper or a hidden evaluator.
- [ ] Implement automatic, dependency-informed lifetime and storage planning, uniquely owned storage, regions/arenas/pools, immutable generations, explicit publication barriers, and protected reader/worker/device epochs or hazard slots as appropriate. These are candidate techniques, not a requirement to implement every technique. Reclaim retired storage only when actual consumers and asynchronous GPU work can no longer access it; a logical DAG alone is not proof of physical object lifetime. Do not disguise reference counts as pins or leases: use independently published reader/worker/device protection and safe quiescence or equivalent non-counting proof. Preserve retention, eviction/reconstruction, recurrence, cancellation and failed-candidate cleanup. Avoid unbounded retention; document progress conditions and bounded-resource failure/backpressure where needed.
- [ ] Provide a design/invariant and allocation/reclamation-path audit: show ownership of buffers and regions, publication/retirement ordering, reader and GPU completion synchronization, stale-handle rejection, safe reuse and eventual reclamation under stated progress assumptions. Cover supported types, dynamic graph replacement, persistent snapshots, multiple concurrent readers, cross-thread and CPU/GPU transfers, effects, failure/cancellation, shutdown and allocation/capacity failure. Native C must not introduce use-after-free, double-free, leaks, invalid aliasing or races.
- [ ] Validate with deterministic adverse interleavings, existing Rust-oracle differential tests, bounded/property tests, allocation failure injection, long-running update/recurrence/eviction/graph-replacement stress, and sanitizer/leak/race checks on applicable native paths (ASan/LSan, UBSan, TSan or documented equivalent). Record live/retired/reclaimed bytes, peak RSS and retention bounds across repeated workloads; demonstrate reclamation during execution, not only at process exit. Test stalled readers and in-flight GPU completion, capacity handling and release after protection ends. Run the existing compiled Radar Chase game with concurrent CPU/GPU execution and repeated replay/resource lifecycle tests under the same policy. Record exact source/compiler/binary provenance.
- [ ] Audit final generated C, DOC-authored support, minimal platform bindings and final linked dependencies for forbidden DOC-lifecycle mechanisms. Explicitly distinguish ordinary OS allocation/synchronization and opaque third-party driver/library internals from DOC-managed lifetimes; no external library may supply GC/RC for DOC-managed storage or replace DOC's lifetime protocol. The temporary Rust bootstrap/reference evaluator may retain its existing safe host-language borrow checker and Arc-based snapshots while needed as an oracle; do not weaken or delete that safety mechanism just to satisfy this policy. It must not be linked or invoked by the final self-hosted runtime/applications. No claim that unrelated OS/driver/library implementation internals are reference-count-free.
- [ ] Preserve all previously required properties: typed checked evaluation, dependency-driven CPU/GPU scaling without application placement hints, reactivity, demand, exact cutoff, recurrence, graph/source generations, immutable published snapshots, protected readers, effects and atomic failure handling. Validate on exact final self-hosted CPU, software-WebGPU and physical-GPU revisions. Do not close #11 on the strength of a scalar/collection subset or a source scan alone.

The abstract DOC semantics remain implementation-neutral; this is a binding conformance restriction on the chosen production realization, not a retroactive proof that every realization of the mathematical model needs no collector or reference counting. If a correctness or practicality counterexample arises, report it and seek an explicit architectural decision rather than silently weakening the restriction. #13 is resolved as a policy decision, with implementation and evidence obligations transferred here. No memory-safety or full self-hosting completion is asserted by that closure.

## PAUSED — graphical game prerequisite
## Active 2D graphical game validation (2026-11-24)
User explicitly paused #11 and resumed the narrow graphical-game portion of #21. Use existing Radar Chase DOC game and the existing WebGPU/WGSL + winit window adapter. No new gameplay in Rust/WGSL, no replacement engine, no authored placement hints. Validate actual window, keyboard movement/spawn/despawn/pause/restart, rendered player/coin/wall/live entities, score/HUD and animation, typed game state and deterministic full replay parity against terminal game. Retain automatic dependency-ready CPU/GPU compute, separate from graphics; verify actual mixed compute and software vs physical adapter labels. Require actual render pixel/frame evidence, not compilation or GPU compute alone. Exercise resize and error handling; maintain existing headless tests. Software Xvfb presentation and physical offscreen rendering/compute are distinct; do not call them physical desktop presentation. Work directly on public rtu0/doc2 main only. Preserve #11 work at 9c17a46696a60994e0042d20da177e639a836e75; do not continue compiler or self-hosting until user authorizes after graphical validation. #10/#22 historical acceptance unchanged. Full editor, generated assets, 3D remain deferred. Final #11 must also preserve the validated graphical game in the self-hosted native realization.
Public tracker: https://github.com/rtu0/doc2/issues/3

## Expanded #21 prerequisite (2026-11-24)
Remain paused until [#21](https://github.com/imxade/DOC/issues/21) / [public #3](https://github.com/rtu0/doc2/issues/3) passes DOC-native declarative 2D and basic 3D graphics and generated WGSL from typed DOC functions, actual graphical Radar Chase, and physical GPU rendering/compute proof. Then #11 must compile these same DOC sources and reproduce graphics and compute semantics without the Rust evaluator, with final non-GC/RC lifetime policy. No resume until user authorizes after readiness.

**Scope correction:** #21's sole new graphical acceptance showcase is now a playable basic 3D DOC-authored game with lighting, simple physics, genuine generated WGSL and automatic CPU/GPU computation. No separate 2D graphical showcase required; keep prior tests as regressions. #11 remains paused and must reproduce the accepted 3D game after self-hosting.
